en.sword: In ancient times, it was unbeatable thanks to its powerful lower body, but it went extinct anyway after it depleted all its plant-based food sources.
en.shield: The powerful muscles in its tail generate its electricity. Compared to its lower body, its upper half is entirely too small.

es.sword: La parte superior del cuerpo está congelada y, al temblar, genera electricidad. Camina con suma dificultad.
es.shield: Antiguamente vivía en el mar y usaba el hielo del cuerpo para conservar los alimentos. Su extrema lentitud, sin embargo, lo condenó a la extinción.

en.sword: The shaking of its freezing upper half is what generates its electricity. It has a hard time walking around.
en.shield: This Pokémon lived on prehistoric seashores and was able to preserve food with the ice on its body. It went extinct because it moved so slowly.

es.sword: Su excelente capacidad motriz y la fuerza de su mandíbula lo hacían antaño invencible, pero dar caza a todas sus presas propició su extinción.
es.shield: Exhibe con orgullo su inmensa capacidad motriz, que le permite superar los 60 km/h, pero solo puede respirar bajo el agua.

en.sword: Powerful legs and jaws made it the apex predator of its time. Its own overhunting of its prey was what drove it to extinction.
en.shield: Its mighty legs are capable of running at speeds exceeding 40 mph, but this Pokémon can’t breathe unless it’s underwater.

es.sword: Atrapa a sus presas congelando su entorno, pero la ubicación de la boca encima de la cabeza le genera dificultades para deglutirlas.
es.shield: Aunque la piel de su rostro era capaz de resistir cualquier ataque, su dificultad para respirar acabó provocando su extinción.

en.sword: Though it’s able to capture prey by freezing its surroundings, it has trouble eating the prey afterward because its mouth is on top of its head.
en.shield: The skin on its face is impervious to attack, but breathing difficulties made this Pokémon go extinct anyway.

es.sword: Su cuerpo, similar a un metal pulido, es tan ligero como robusto. Sin embargo, tiene el defecto de que se oxida con facilidad.
es.shield: Hace gala de una agilidad extraordinaria, ya que su cuerpo está compuesto de un metal especial. Detesta la lluvia, por lo que habita en cuevas.

en.sword: Its body resembles polished metal, and it’s both lightweight and strong. The only drawback is that it rusts easily.
en.shield: The special metal that composes its body is very light, so this Pokémon has considerable agility. It lives in caves because it dislikes the rain.

es.sword: Habitaba los mares en tiempos inmemoriales. Ha revivido en forma de Pokémon de tipo Fantasma para vagar por su antigua morada.
es.shield: En solitario es tan débil que no sería rival ni para un niño, pero, al entrenarse con sus congéneres, evoluciona y se vuelve más fuerte.

en.sword: After being reborn as a ghost Pokémon, Dreepy wanders the areas it used to inhabit back when it was alive in prehistoric seas.
en.shield: If this weak Pokémon is by itself, a mere child could defeat it. But if Dreepy has friends to help it train, it can evolve and become much stronger.

es.sword: Vuela a una velocidad de 200 km/h. Lucha junto a un Dreepy, al que cuida hasta el momento de su evolución.
es.shield: Si no lleva un Dreepy del que cuidar encima de la cabeza, se intranquiliza y trata de sustituirlo con otro Pokémon.

en.sword: It’s capable of flying faster than 120 mph. It battles alongside Dreepy and dotes on them until they successfully evolve.
en.shield: Without a Dreepy to place on its head and care for, it gets so uneasy it’ll try to substitute any Pokémon it finds for the missing Dreepy.

es.sword: Vive en compañía de Dreepy, a los que hospeda en el interior de sus cuernos. Los dispara a velocidad supersónica en combate.
es.shield: Al parecer, los Dreepy que residen en sus cuernos esperan con ilusión el momento de ser propulsados a velocidad supersónica.

en.sword: When it isn’t battling, it keeps Dreepy in the holes on its horns. Once a fight starts, it launches the Dreepy like supersonic missiles.
en.shield: Apparently the Dreepy inside Dragapult’s horns eagerly look forward to being launched out at Mach speeds.

es.sword: Este Pokémon está considerado como un héroe de leyenda. Absorbe el metal para transformarlo y emplearlo como armamento.
es.shield: Hay quien lo considera una suerte de figura fraterna a la par que rival de Zamazenta, un Pokémon sumido en un profundo letargo.

en.sword: Known as a legendary hero, this Pokémon absorbs metal particles, transforming them into a weapon it uses to battle.
en.shield: This Pokémon has slumbered for many years. Some say it’s Zamazenta’s elder sister—others say the two Pokémon are rivals.

es.sword: Este Pokémon se erigió en salvador de Galar, tras unir fuerzas con un rey de los hombres. Absorbe el metal para utilizarlo en combate.
es.shield: Con la apariencia de una estatua de piedra, este Pokémon se sumió en un letargo tan profundo que acabó cayendo en el olvido.

en.sword: In times past, it worked together with a king of the people to save the Galar region. It absorbs metal that it then uses in battle.
en.shield: This Pokémon slept for aeons while in the form of a statue. It was asleep for so long, people forgot that it ever existed.

es.sword: Se alimenta de la energía que brota de la tierra de Galar absorbiéndola por el núcleo del pecho.
es.shield: Fue hallado en el interior de un meteorito caído hace 20 000 años. Por lo visto, está relacionado con el misterio que rodea al fenómeno Dinamax.

en.sword: The core on its chest absorbs energy emanating from the lands of the Galar region. This energy is what allows Eternatus to stay active.
en.shield: It was inside a meteorite that fell 20,000 years ago. There seems to be a connection between this Pokémon and the Dynamax phenomenon.

es.sword: Perfecciona su técnica mediante una estricta disciplina. Según la corriente marcial que siga, adoptará una forma u otra al evolucionar.
es.shield: Al tirar de los mechones blancos de la cabeza, acrecienta su espíritu luchador y empieza a acumular fuerza en el órgano de su bajo vientre.

en.sword: Kubfu trains hard to perfect its moves. The moves it masters will determine which form it takes when it evolves.
en.shield: If Kubfu pulls the long white hair on its head, its fighting spirit heightens and power wells up from the depths of its belly.

es.sword: Su estilo de lucha se basa en abatir a sus rivales de un solo golpe. Se abalanza sobre ellos con su puño cincelado por el entrenamiento.
es.shield: Vive en zonas montañosas en áreas recónditas, donde entrena corriendo por escarpados riscos para fortalecer sus piernas y refinar su técnica.

en.sword: This form of Urshifu is a strong believer in the one-hit KO. Its strategy is to leap in close to foes and land a devastating blow with a hardened fist.
en.shield: Inhabiting the mountains of a distant region, this Pokémon races across sheer cliffs, training its legs and refining its moves.

es.sword: Viven en manada en la selva. Debido a su marcada agresividad, son muy temidos por otros Pokémon selváticos.
es.shield: Las lianas que le brotan del cuerpo nutren y fertilizan el mantillo del bosque cuando se le desprenden.

en.sword: Within dense forests, this Pokémon lives in a pack with others of its kind. It’s incredibly aggressive, and the other Pokémon of the forest fear it.
en.shield: Once the vines on Zarude’s body tear off, they become nutrients in the soil. This helps the plants of the forest grow.

es.sword: Su cuerpo entero es energía eléctrica. Por lo visto, quitarle los anillos que lleva libera su poder oculto.
es.shield: Todo su cuerpo es un órgano electrógeno, cuya potencia sería suficiente para abastecer la región de Galar por completo.

en.sword: This Pokémon is a cluster of electrical energy. It’s said that removing the rings on Regieleki’s body will unleash the Pokémon’s latent power.
en.shield: Its entire body is made up of a single organ that generates electrical energy. Regieleki is capable of creating all Galar’s electricity.

es.sword: Cierta teoría afirma que la forma de sus brazos representa la cabeza de un Pokémon dragón ancestral, aunque esto no ha podido verificarse.
es.shield: Todo su cuerpo es una gema de energía dragón cristalizada. Se cree que posee los poderes de todos los Pokémon dragón.

en.sword: An academic theory proposes that Regidrago’s arms were once the head of an ancient dragon Pokémon. The theory remains unproven.
en.shield: Its body is composed of crystallized dragon energy. Regidrago is said to have the powers of every dragon Pokémon.

es.sword: Libera un potente vaho gélido por las pezuñas. Un ser violento que no duda en tomar a la fuerza todo cuanto desea.
es.shield: Cuenta con una fuerza física sobrecogedora. La máscara de hielo que le cubre el rostro es cien veces más dura que el diamante.

en.sword: Glastrier emits intense cold from its hooves. It’s also a belligerent Pokémon—anything it wants, it takes by force.
en.shield: Glastrier has tremendous physical strength, and the mask of ice covering its face is 100 times harder than diamond.

es.sword: Examina su entorno con todos los sentidos, salvo la vista. Se dice que sus coces son capaces de robarle el alma a quien las recibe.
es.shield: Amante de la quietud y la soledad, galopa por las tinieblas nocturnas absorbiendo la energía vital de toda criatura que esté durmiendo.

en.sword: It probes its surroundings with all its senses save one—it doesn’t use its sense of sight. Spectrier’s kicks are said to separate soul from body.
en.shield: As it dashes through the night, Spectrier absorbs the life-force of sleeping creatures. It craves silence and solitude.

es.sword: Un Pokémon muy compasivo agraciado con el poder de la curación. Reinó en Galar en tiempos remotos.
es.shield: Legendario monarca del antiguo Galar. Posee el poder de sanar el espíritu y de hacer brotar la vegetación.

en.sword: Calyrex is a merciful Pokémon, capable of providing healing and blessings. It reigned over the Galar region in times of yore.
en.shield: Calyrex is known in legend as a king that ruled over Galar in ancient times. It has the power to cause hearts to mend and plants to spring forth.

en.legends-arceus: The black orbs shine with an uncanny light when the Pokémon is erecting invisible barriers. The fur shed from its beard retains heat well and is a highly useful material for winter clothing.
A violent creature that fells towering trees with its crude axes and shields itself with hard stone. If one should chance upon this Pokémon in the wilds, one's only recourse is to flee.
I believe it was Hisui's swampy terrain that gave Ursaluna its burly physique and newfound capacity to manipulate peat at will.
Clads itself in the souls of comrades that perished before fulfilling their goals of journeying upstream. No other species throughout all Hisui's rivers is Basculegion's equal.
Because of Sneasler's virulent poison and daunting physical prowess, no other species could hope to best it on the frozen highlands. Preferring solitude, this species does not form packs.
Its lancelike spikes and savage temperament have earned it the nickname ”sea fiend.” It slurps up poison to nourish itself.
When it flies to this land from across the sea, the bitter winter comes to an end. According to legend, this Pokémon's love gives rise to the budding of fresh life across Hisui.

en.scarlet: Its fluffy fur is similar in composition to plants. This Pokémon frequently washes its face to keep it from drying out.
en.violet: The sweet scent its body gives off mesmerizes those around it. The scent grows stronger when this Pokémon is in the sun.

en.scarlet: Floragato deftly wields the vine hidden beneath its long fur, slamming the hard flower bud against its opponents.
en.violet: The hardness of Floragato’s fur depends on the Pokémon’s mood. When Floragato is prepared to battle, its fur becomes pointed and needle sharp.

en.scarlet: This Pokémon uses the reflective fur lining its cape to camouflage the stem of its flower, creating the illusion that the flower is floating.
en.violet: With skillful misdirection, it rigs foes with pollen-packed flower bombs. Meowscarada sets off the bombs before its foes realize what’s going on.

en.scarlet: It lies on warm rocks and uses the heat absorbed by its square-shaped scales to create fire energy.
en.violet: Its flame sac is small, so energy is always leaking out. This energy is released from the dent atop Fuecoco’s head and flickers to and fro.

en.scarlet: The combination of Crocalor’s fire energy and overflowing vitality has caused an egg-shaped fireball to appear on the Pokémon’s head.
en.violet: The valve in Crocalor’s flame sac is closely connected to its vocal cords. This Pokémon utters a guttural cry as it spews flames every which way.

en.scarlet: The fiery bird changes shape when Skeledirge sings. Rumor has it that the bird was born when the fireball on Skeledirge’s head gained a soul.
en.violet: Skeledirge’s gentle singing soothes the souls of all that hear it. It burns its enemies to a crisp with flames of over 5,400 degrees Fahrenheit.

en.scarlet: This Pokémon migrated to Paldea from distant lands long ago. The gel secreted by its feathers repels water and grime.
en.violet: Its strong legs let it easily swim around in even fast-flowing rivers. It likes to keep things tidy and is prone to overthinking things.

en.scarlet: These Pokémon constantly run through shallow waters to train their legs, then compete with each other to see which of them kicks most gracefully.
en.violet: The hardworking Quaxwell observes people and Pokémon from various regions and incorporates their movements into its own dance routines.

en.scarlet: A single kick from a Quaquaval can send a truck rolling. This Pokémon uses its powerful legs to perform striking dances from far-off lands.
en.violet: Dancing in ways that evoke far-away places, this Pokémon mesmerizes all that see it. Flourishes of its decorative water feathers slice into its foes.

en.scarlet: It searches for food all day. It possesses a keen sense of smell but doesn’t use it for anything other than foraging.
en.violet: This Pokémon spurns all but the finest of foods. Its body gives off an herblike scent that bug Pokémon detest.

en.scarlet: Oinkologne is proud of its fine, glossy skin. It emits a concentrated scent from the tip of its tail.
en.violet: It entrances female Pokémon with the sweet, alluring scent that wafts from all over its body.

en.scarlet: The ball of threads wrapped around its body is elastic enough to deflect the scythes of Scyther, this Pokémon’s natural enemy.
en.violet: The thread it secretes from its rear is as strong as wire. The secret behind the thread’s strength is the topic of ongoing research.

en.scarlet: It clings to branches and ceilings using its threads and moves without a sound. It takes out its prey before the prey even notices it.
en.violet: Spidops covers its territory in tough, sticky threads to set up traps for intruders.

en.scarlet: It has its third set of legs folded up. When it’s in a tough spot, this Pokémon jumps over 30 feet using the strength of its legs.
en.violet: It’s highly skilled at a fighting style in which it uses its jumping capabilities to dodge incoming attacks while also dealing damage to opponents.

en.scarlet: When it decides to fight all out, it stands on its previously folded legs to enter Showdown Mode. It neutralizes its enemies in short order.
en.violet: It uses its normally folded third set of legs when in Showdown Mode. This places a huge burden on its body, so it can’t stay in this mode for long.

en.scarlet: It has underdeveloped electric sacs on its cheeks. These sacs can produce electricity only if Pawmi rubs them furiously with the pads on its forepaws.
en.violet: The pads of its paws are electricity-discharging organs. Pawmi fires electricity from its forepaws while standing unsteadily on its hind legs.

en.scarlet: When its group is attacked, Pawmo is the first to leap into battle, defeating enemies with a fighting technique that utilizes electric shocks.
en.violet: Pawmo uses a unique fighting technique in which it uses its forepaws to strike foes and zap them with electricity from its paw pads simultaneously.

en.scarlet: This Pokémon normally is slow to react, but once it enters battle, it will strike down its enemies with lightning-fast movements.
en.violet: Pawmot’s fluffy fur acts as a battery. It can store the same amount of electricity as an electric car.

en.scarlet: Exhibiting great teamwork, they use their incisors to cut pieces out of any material that might be useful for a nest, then make off with them.
en.violet: The pair sticks together no matter what. They split any food they find exactly in half and then eat it together.

en.scarlet: The two little ones just appeared one day. The group might be a family of related Pokémon, but nobody knows for sure.
en.violet: The larger pair protects the little ones during battles. When facing strong opponents, the whole group will join the fight.

en.scarlet: This Pokémon is smooth and moist to the touch. Yeast in Fidough’s breath induces fermentation in the Pokémon’s vicinity.
en.violet: The yeast in Fidough’s breath is useful for cooking, so this Pokémon has been protected by people since long ago.

en.scarlet: The pleasant aroma that emanates from this Pokémon’s body helps wheat grow, so Dachsbun has been treasured by farming villages.
en.violet: The surface of this Pokémon’s skin hardens when exposed to intense heat, and its body has an appetizing aroma.

en.scarlet: It protects itself from enemies by emitting oil from the fruit on its head. This oil is bitter and astringent enough to make someone flinch.
en.violet: This Pokémon converts nutrients into oil, which it stores in the fruit on its head. It can easily go a whole week without eating or drinking.

en.scarlet: Dolliv shares its tasty, fresh-scented oil with others. This species has coexisted with humans since times long gone.
en.violet: It basks in the sun to its heart’s content until the fruits on its head ripen. After that, Dolliv departs from human settlements and goes on a journey.

en.scarlet: This calm Pokémon is very compassionate. It will share its delicious, nutrient-rich oil with weakened Pokémon.
en.violet: This Pokémon drives back enemies by launching its rich, aromatic oil at them with enough force to smash a boulder.

en.scarlet: These Pokémon prefer to live in cities. They form flocks based on the color of their feathers, and they fight over territory.
en.violet: Green-feathered flocks hold the most sway. When they’re out searching for food in the mornings and evenings, it gets very noisy.

en.scarlet: It was born in a layer of rock salt deep under the earth. This species was particularly treasured in the old days, as they would share precious salt.
en.violet: The ground scrapes its body as it travels, causing it to leave salt behind. Salt is constantly being created and replenished inside Nacli’s body.

en.scarlet: This Pokémon dry cures its prey by spraying salt over them. The curing process steals away the water in the prey’s body.
en.violet: It compresses rock salt inside its body and shoots out hardened salt pellets with enough force to perforate an iron sheet.

en.scarlet: Garganacl will rub its fingertips together and sprinkle injured Pokémon with salt. Even severe wounds will promptly heal afterward.
en.violet: Many Pokémon gather around Garganacl, hoping to lick at its mineral-rich salt.

en.scarlet: Burnt charcoal came to life and became a Pokémon. Possessing a fiery fighting spirit, Charcadet will battle even tough opponents.
en.violet: Its firepower increases when it fights, reaching over 1,800 degrees Fahrenheit. It likes berries that are rich in fat.

en.scarlet: Armarouge evolved through the use of a set of armor that belonged to a distinguished warrior. This Pokémon is incredibly loyal.
en.violet: This Pokémon clads itself in armor that has been fortified by psychic and fire energy, and it shoots blazing fireballs.

en.scarlet: The fiery blades on its arms burn fiercely with the lingering resentment of a sword wielder who fell before accomplishing their goal.
en.violet: An old set of armor steeped in grudges caused this Pokémon’s evolution. Ceruledge cuts its enemies to pieces without mercy.

en.scarlet: Tadbulb shakes its tail to generate electricity. If it senses danger, it will make its head blink on and off to alert its allies.
en.violet: It floats using the electricity stored in its body. When thunderclouds are around, Tadbulb will float higher off the ground.

en.scarlet: When this Pokémon expands and contracts its wobbly body, the belly-button dynamo in its stomach produces a huge amount of electricity.
en.violet: What appear to be eyeballs are actually organs for discharging the electricity generated by Bellibolt’s belly-button dynamo.

en.scarlet: When its wings catch the wind, the bones within produce electricity. This Pokémon dives into the ocean, catching prey by electrocuting them.
en.violet: These Pokémon make their nests on coastal cliffs. The nests have a strange, crackling texture, and they’re a popular delicacy.

en.scarlet: Kilowattrel inflates its throat sac to amplify its electricity. By riding the wind, this Pokémon can fly over 430 miles in a day.
en.violet: It uses its throat sac to store electricity generated by its wings. There’s hardly any oil in its feathers, so it is a poor swimmer.

en.scarlet: It always scowls in an attempt to make opponents take it seriously, but even crying children will burst into laughter when they see Maschiff’s face.
en.violet: Its well-developed jaw and fangs are strong enough to crunch through boulders, and its thick fat makes for an excellent defense.

en.scarlet: This Pokémon can store energy in its large dewlap. Mabosstiff unleashes this energy all at once to blow away enemies.
en.violet: Mabosstiff loves playing with children. Though usually gentle, it takes on an intimidating look when protecting its family.

en.scarlet: Though usually a mellow Pokémon, it will sink its sharp, poison-soaked front teeth into any that anger it, causing paralysis in the object of its ire.
en.violet: To keep enemies away from its territory, it paints markings around its nest using a poisonous liquid that has an acrid odor.

en.scarlet: The color of the poisonous saliva depends on what the Pokémon eats. Grafaiai covers its fingers in its saliva and draws patterns on trees in forests.
en.violet: Each Grafaiai paints its own individual pattern, and it will paint that same pattern over and over again throughout its life.

en.scarlet: A soul unable to move on to the afterlife was blown around by the wind until it got tangled up with dried grass and became a Pokémon.
en.violet: Not even Bramblin knows where it is headed as it tumbles across the wilderness, blown by the wind. It loathes getting wet.

en.scarlet: It will open the branches of its head to envelop its prey. Once it absorbs all the life energy it needs, it expels the prey and discards it.
en.violet: Brambleghast wanders around arid regions. On rare occasions, mass outbreaks of these Pokémon will bury an entire town.

en.scarlet: Toedscool lives in muggy forests. The flaps that fall from its body are chewy and very delicious.
en.violet: Though it looks like Tentacool, Toedscool is a completely different species. Its legs may be thin, but it can run at a speed of 30 mph.

en.scarlet: These Pokémon gather into groups and form colonies deep within forests. They absolutely hate it when strangers approach.
en.violet: It coils its 10 tentacles around prey and sucks out their nutrients, causing the prey pain. The folds along the rim of its head are a popular delicacy.

en.scarlet: Klawf hangs upside-down from cliffs, waiting for prey. But Klawf can’t remain in this position for long because its blood rushes to its head.
en.violet: This Pokémon lives on sheer cliffs. It sidesteps opponents’ attacks, then lunges for their weak spots with its claws.

en.scarlet: The more sunlight this Pokémon bathes in, the more spicy chemicals are produced by its body, and thus the spicier its moves become.
en.violet: Traditional Paldean dishes can be extremely spicy because they include the shed front teeth of Capsakid among their ingredients.

en.scarlet: The red head converts spicy chemicals into fire energy and blasts the surrounding area with a super spicy stream of flame.
en.violet: The green head has turned vicious due to the spicy chemicals stimulating its brain. Once it goes on a rampage, there is no stopping it.

en.scarlet: This Pokémon creates a mud ball by mixing sand and dirt with psychic energy. It treasures its mud ball more than its own life.
en.violet: It rolls its mud ball around while the energy it needs for evolution matures. Eventually the time comes for it to evolve.

en.scarlet: The body that supports the ball barely moves. Therefore, it is thought that the true body of this Pokémon is actually inside the ball.
en.violet: An infant sleeps inside the ball. Rabsca rolls the ball soothingly with its legs to ensure the infant sleeps comfortably.

en.scarlet: Flittle’s toes levitate about half an inch above the ground because of the psychic power emitted from the frills on the Pokémon’s belly.
en.violet: It spends its time running around wastelands. If anyone steals its beloved berries, it will chase them down and exact its revenge.

en.scarlet: It immobilizes opponents by bathing them in psychic power from its large eyes. Despite its appearance, it has a vicious temperament.
en.violet: It emits psychic power from the gaps between its multicolored frills and sprints at speeds greater than 120 mph.

en.scarlet: It swings its handmade hammer around to protect itself, but the hammer is often stolen by Pokémon that eat metal.
en.violet: This Pokémon pounds iron scraps together to make a hammer. It will remake the hammer again and again until it’s satisfied with the result.

en.scarlet: This Pokémon will attack groups of Pawniard and Bisharp, gathering metal from them in order to create a large and sturdy hammer.
en.violet: These Pokémon make their homes in piles of scrap metal. They test the strength of each other’s hammers by smashing them together.

en.scarlet: This intelligent Pokémon has a very daring disposition. It knocks rocks into the sky with its hammer, aiming for flying Corviknight.
en.violet: The hammer tops 220 pounds, yet it gets swung around easily by Tinkaton as it steals whatever it pleases and carries its plunder back home.

en.scarlet: This Pokémon can pick up the scent of a Veluza just over 65 feet away and will hide itself in the sand.
en.violet: Though it looks like Diglett, Wiglett is an entirely different species. The resemblance seems to be a coincidental result of environmental adaptation.

en.scarlet: It has a vicious temperament, contrary to what its appearance may suggest. It wraps its long bodies around prey, then drags the prey into its den.
en.violet: A variety of fish Pokémon, Wugtrio was once considered to be a regional form of Dugtrio.

en.scarlet: It gathers things up in an apron made from shed feathers added to the Pokémon’s chest feathers, then drops those things from high places for fun.
en.violet: Bombirdier uses the apron on its chest to bundle up food, which it carries back to its nest. It enjoys dropping things that make loud noises.

en.scarlet: It likes playing with others of its kind using the water ring on its tail. It uses ultrasonic waves to sense the emotions of other living creatures.
en.violet: Its water ring is made from seawater mixed with a sticky fluid that Finizen secretes from its blowhole.

en.scarlet: This Pokémon changes its appearance if it hears its allies calling for help. Palafin will never show anybody its moment of transformation.
en.violet: Its physical capabilities are no different than a Finizen’s, but when its allies are in danger, it transforms and powers itself up.

en.scarlet: It is said that this Pokémon was born when an unknown poison Pokémon entered and inspirited an engine left at a scrap-processing factory.
en.violet: The steel section is Varoom’s actual body. This Pokémon clings to rocks and converts the minerals within into energy to fuel its activities.

en.scarlet: It creates a gas out of poison and minerals from rocks. It then detonates the gas in its cylinders—now numbering eight—to generate energy.
en.violet: Revavroom viciously threatens others with the sound of its exhaust. It sticks its tongue out from its cylindrical mouth and sprays toxic fluids.

en.scarlet: Apparently Cyclizar has been allowing people to ride on its back since ancient times. Depictions of this have been found in 10,000-year-old murals.
en.violet: It can sprint at over 70 mph while carrying a human. The rider’s body heat warms Cyclizar’s back and lifts the Pokémon’s spirit.

en.scarlet: When attacked, this Pokémon will wield the tendrils on its body like fists and pelt the opponent with a storm of punches.
en.violet: This Pokémon lives in arid deserts. It maintains its metal body by consuming iron from the soil.

en.scarlet: It absorbs nutrients from cave walls. The petals it wears are made of crystallized poison.
en.violet: Glimmet’s toxic mineral crystals look just like flower petals. This Pokémon scatters poisonous powder like pollen to protect itself.

en.scarlet: When this Pokémon detects danger, it will open up its crystalline petals and fire beams from its conical body.
en.violet: Glimmora’s petals are made of crystallized poison energy. It has recently become evident that these petals resemble Tera Jewels.

en.scarlet: It is said that a dog Pokémon that died in the wild without ever interacting with a human was reborn as this Pokémon.
en.violet: This friendly Pokémon doesn’t like being alone. Pay it even the slightest bit of attention, and it will follow you forever.

en.scarlet: Houndstone spends most of its time sleeping in graveyards. Among all the dog Pokémon, this one is most loyal to its master.
en.violet: A lovingly mourned Pokémon was reborn as Houndstone. It doesn’t like anyone touching the protuberance atop its head.

en.scarlet: This Pokémon apparently ties the base of its neck into a knot so that energy stored in its belly does not escape from its beak.
en.violet: Thanks to a behavior of theirs known as “synchronizing,” an entire flock of these Pokémon can attack simultaneously in perfect harmony.

en.scarlet: This species left the ocean and began living on land a very long time ago. It seems to be closely related to Wailmer.
en.violet: It lives in frigid regions in pods of five or so individuals. It loves the minerals found in snow and ice.

en.scarlet: This Pokémon wanders around snowy, icy areas. It protects its body with powerful muscles and a thick layer of fat under its skin.
en.violet: Ice energy builds up in the horn on its upper jaw, causing the horn to reach cryogenic temperatures that freeze its surroundings.

en.scarlet: When Veluza discards unnecessary flesh, its mind becomes honed and its psychic power increases. The spare flesh has a mild but delicious flavor.
en.violet: Veluza has excellent regenerative capabilities. It sheds spare flesh from its body to boost its agility, then charges at its prey.

en.scarlet: This Pokémon is a glutton, but it’s bad at getting food. It teams up with a Tatsugiri to catch prey.
en.violet: It treats Tatsugiri like its boss and follows it loyally. Though powerful, Dondozo is apparently not very smart.

en.scarlet: This is a small dragon Pokémon. It lives inside the mouth of Dondozo to protect itself from enemies on the outside.
en.violet: Tatsugiri is an extremely cunning Pokémon. It feigns weakness to lure in prey, then orders its partner to attack.

en.scarlet: When its anger rose beyond a critical point, this Pokémon gained power that is unfettered by the limits of its physical body.
en.violet: It imbues its fists with the power of the rage that it kept hidden in its heart. Opponents struck by these imbued fists will be shattered to their core.

en.scarlet: When attacked, this Pokémon will retaliate by sticking thick spines out from its body. It’s a risky move that puts everything on the line.
en.violet: It lives at the bottom of ponds and swamps. It will carry Wooper on its back and ferry them across water from one shore to the other.

en.scarlet: Now that the brain waves from the head and tail are synced up, the psychic power of this Pokémon is 10 times stronger than Girafarig’s.
en.violet: The hardened head from the tail protects the head of the main body as Farigiraf whips its long neck around to headbutt enemies.

en.scarlet: This Pokémon uses its hard tail to make its nest by boring holes into bedrock deep underground. The nest can reach lengths of over six miles.
en.violet: It drives enemies out of its nest by sucking in enough air to fill its long, narrow lungs, then releasing the air in an intense blast.

en.scarlet: Only a Bisharp that stands above all others in its vast army can evolve into Kingambit.
en.violet: Though it commands a massive army in battle, it’s not skilled at devising complex strategies. It just uses brute strength to keep pushing.

en.scarlet: Sightings of this Pokémon have occurred in recent years. The name Great Tusk was taken from a creature listed in a certain book.
en.violet: This creature resembles a mysterious Pokémon that, according to a paranormal magazine, has lived since ancient times.

en.scarlet: There has been only one reported sighting of this Pokémon. It resembles a mysterious creature depicted in an old expedition journal.
en.violet: It resembles a mysterious Pokémon described in a paranormal magazine as a Jigglypuff from one billion years ago.

en.scarlet: It is possible that the creature listed as Brute Bonnet in a certain book could actually be this Pokémon.
en.violet: It bears a slight resemblance to a Pokémon described in a dubious magazine as a cross between a dinosaur and a mushroom.

en.scarlet: This Pokémon has characteristics similar to those of Flutter Mane, a creature mentioned in a certain book.
en.violet: It has similar features to a ghostly pterosaur that was covered in a paranormal magazine, but the two have little else in common.

en.scarlet: This mysterious Pokémon has some similarities to a creature that an old book introduced as Slither Wing.
en.violet: This Pokémon somewhat resembles an ancient form of Volcarona that was introduced in a dubious magazine.
It slightly resembles a Magneton that lived for 10,000 years and was featured in an article in a paranormal magazine.
en.scarlet: No records exist of this Pokémon being caught. Data is lacking, but the Pokémon’s traits match up with a creature shown in an expedition journal.
This Pokémon closely resembles a scientific weapon that a paranormal magazine claimed was sent to this planet by aliens.
en.violet: Sightings of this Pokémon have occurred in recent years. It resembles a mysterious object described in an old expedition journal.

en.scarlet: Its shape is similar to a robot featured in a paranormal magazine article. The robot was said to have been created by an ancient civilization.
en.violet: It resembles a mysterious object mentioned in an old book. There are only two reported sightings of this Pokémon.

en.scarlet: It is very similar to a cyborg covered exclusively by a paranormal magazine. The cyborg was said to be the modified form of a certain athlete.
en.violet: This Pokémon shares many similarities with Iron Hands, an object mentioned in a certain expedition journal.

en.scarlet: It resembles a certain Pokémon introduced in a paranormal magazine, described as the offspring of a Hydreigon that fell in love with a robot.
en.violet: It’s possible that Iron Jugulis, an object described in an old book, may actually be this Pokémon.

en.scarlet: This Pokémon resembles an unknown object described in a paranormal magazine as a UFO sent to observe humanity.
en.violet: No records exist of this species being caught. Data is lacking, but the Pokémon’s traits match up with an object described in an old book.

en.scarlet: It has some similarities to a Pokémon introduced in a dubious magazine as a Tyranitar from one billion years into the future.
en.violet: Some of its notable features match those of an object named within a certain expedition journal as Iron Thorns.

en.scarlet: Frigibax absorbs heat through its dorsal fin and converts the heat into ice energy. The higher the temperature, the more energy Frigibax stores.
en.violet: This Pokémon lives in forests and craggy areas. Using the power of its dorsal fin, it cools the inside of its nest like a refrigerator.

en.scarlet: Arctibax freezes the air around it, protecting its face with an ice mask and turning its dorsal fin into a blade of ice.
en.violet: It attacks with the blade of its frozen dorsal fin by doing a front flip in the air. Arctibax’s strong back and legs allow it to pull off this technique.

en.scarlet: This Pokémon blasts cryogenic air out from its mouth. This air can instantly freeze even liquid-hot lava.
en.violet: It launches itself into battle by flipping upside down and spewing frigid air from its mouth. It finishes opponents off with its dorsal blade.

en.scarlet: This Pokémon was born inside a treasure chest about 1,500 years ago. It sucks the life-force out of scoundrels who try to steal the treasure.
en.violet: It lives inside an old treasure chest. Sometimes it gets left in shop corners since no one realizes it’s actually a Pokémon.

en.scarlet: Its body seems to be made up of 1,000 coins. This Pokémon gets along well with others and is quick to make friends with anybody.
en.violet: It has a sturdy body made up of stacked coins. Gholdengo overwhelms its enemies by firing coin after coin at them in quick succession.

en.scarlet: The grudge of a person punished for writing the king’s evil deeds upon wooden tablets has clad itself in dead leaves to become a Pokémon.
en.violet: It drains the life-force from vegetation, causing nearby forests to instantly wither and fields to turn barren.

en.scarlet: This Pokémon can control 100 tons of fallen snow. It plays around innocently by leaping in and out of avalanches it has caused.
en.violet: The hatred of those who perished by the sword long ago has clad itself in snow and become a Pokémon.

en.scarlet: The fear poured into an ancient ritual vessel has clad itself in rocks and dirt to become a Pokémon.
en.violet: It slowly brings its exceedingly heavy head down upon the ground, splitting the earth open with huge fissures that run over 160 feet deep.

en.scarlet: It controls flames burning at over 5,400 degrees Fahrenheit. It casually swims through the sea of lava it creates by melting rock and sand.
en.violet: The envy accumulated within curved beads that sparked multiple conflicts has clad itself in fire and become a Pokémon.

en.scarlet: It is possible that this is the creature listed as Roaring Moon in an expedition journal that still holds many mysteries.
en.violet: According to an article in a dubious magazine, this Pokémon has some connection to a phenomenon that occurs in a certain region.

en.scarlet: It has some similarities to a mad scientist’s invention covered in a paranormal magazine.
en.violet: It’s possible that this is the object listed as Iron Valiant in a certain expedition journal.

en.scarlet: This seems to be the Winged King mentioned in an old expedition journal. It was said to have split the land with its bare fists.
en.violet: This Pokémon resembles Cyclizar, but it is far burlier and more ferocious. Nothing is known about its ecology or other features.

en.scarlet: Much remains unknown about this creature. It resembles Cyclizar, but it is far more ruthless and powerful.
en.violet: This seems to be the Iron Serpent mentioned in an old book. The Iron Serpent is said to have turned the land to ash with its lightning.

en.scarlet: This ferocious creature is shrouded in mystery. It's named after an aquatic monster mentioned in an old expedition journal.
en.violet: It resembles an illustration published in a paranormal magazine, said to be a depiction of a super-ancient Suicune.

en.scarlet: Many of its physical characteristics match those of a Virizion from the future that was covered in a paranormal magazine.
en.violet: According to the few eyewitness accounts that exist, it used its shining blades to julienne large trees and boulders.

en.scarlet: Dipplin is two creatures in one Pokémon. Its evolution was triggered by a special apple grown only in one place.
en.violet: The head sticking out belongs to the fore-wyrm, while the tail belongs to the core-wyrm. The two share one apple and help each other out.

en.scarlet: Supposedly, the regrets of a tea ceremony master who died before perfecting his craft lingered in some matcha and became a Pokémon.
en.violet: Poltchageist looks like a regional form of Sinistea, but it was recently discovered that the two Pokémon are entirely unrelated.

en.scarlet: It pretends to be tea, trying to fool people into drinking it so it can drain their life-force. Its ruse is generally unsuccessful.
en.violet: It prefers cool, dark places, such as the back of a shelf or the space beneath a home's floorboards. It wanders in search of prey after sunset.

en.scarlet: After all its muscles were stimulated by the toxic chain around its neck, Okidogi transformed and gained a powerful physique.
en.violet: Okidogi is a ruffian with a short temper. It can pulverize anything by swinging around the chain on its neck.

en.scarlet: The chain is made from toxins that enhance capabilities. It stimulated Munkidori's brain and caused the Pokémon's psychic powers to bloom.
en.violet: Munkidori keeps itself somewhere safe while it toys with its foes, using psychokinesis to induce intense dizziness.

en.scarlet: Fezandipiti owes its beautiful looks and lovely voice to the toxic stimulants emanating from the chain wrapped around its body.
en.violet: Fezandipiti beats its glossy wings to scatter pheromones that captivate people and Pokémon.

en.scarlet: This Pokémon's type changes based on which mask it's wearing. It confounds its enemies with nimble movements and kicks.
en.violet: This mischief-loving Pokémon is full of curiosity. It battles by drawing out the type-based energy contained within its masks.

en.scarlet: It gathers static electricity from its surroundings. The beams it launches when down on all fours are tremendously powerful.
en.violet: It digs holes on mountains, searching for food. It’s so durable that being caught in a cave-in won’t faze it.

en.scarlet: Seven syrpents live inside an apple made of syrup. The syrpent in the center is the commander.
en.violet: These capricious syrpents have banded together. On the rare occasion that their moods align, their true power is unleashed.

en.scarlet: There are scant few reports of this creature being sighted. One short video shows it rampaging and spouting pillars of flame.
en.violet: It resembles an eerie Pokémon once shown in a paranormal magazine. That Pokémon was said to be an Entei regenerated from a fossil.

en.scarlet: It's said to incinerate everything around it with lightning launched from its fur. Very little is known about this creature.
en.violet: It bears resemblance to a Pokémon that became a hot topic for a short while after a paranormal magazine touted it as Raikou's ancestor.

en.scarlet: It resembles a Pokémon described in a dubious magazine as a Terrakion that had been modified by an evil organization.
en.violet: It was named after a mysterious object recorded in an old book. Its body seems to be metallic.

en.scarlet: It resembles a mysterious object introduced in a paranormal magazine as a cutting-edge weapon shaped like a Cobalion.
en.violet: There was supposedly an incident in which it launched shining blades to cut everything around it to pieces. Little else is known about it.

en.scarlet: Terapagos protects itself using its power to transform energy into hard crystals. This Pokémon is the source of the Terastal phenomenon.
en.violet: It’s thought that this Pokémon lived in ancient Paldea until it got caught in seismic shifts and went extinct.

en.scarlet: It feeds others toxic mochi that draw out desires and capabilities. Those who eat the mochi fall under Pecharunt’s control, chained to its will.
en.violet: Its peach-shaped shell serves as storage for a potent poison. It makes poisonous mochi and serves them to people and Pokémon.
